Both make true knowing the end of suffering: the Kural's one who knows the support and lives so that clinging ends is not touched by the pains, Tirumular's who have awareness have no suffering.
Both describe the union by the image of flesh, or body, and the life within it, and both deny any 'I' and 'you' apart.
Both name the Lord அறவாழி அந்தணன். In the Kural only those who reach his feet cross the other seas; in Tirumular he himself gives the way of no birth and comes into the heart as kin.
Both give the Lord the five acts. 1927 says it of the Supreme as seed and root of cause and effect; 1809 says it with தானே in every line, adding that he also grants release.
1807 lists the nine forms he dances as; 1810 sorts them into four formless, Sadasiva as form-formless, and four with form, while keeping him one.
Both make bindu the source that becomes Mahamaya and all the worlds; 1813 adds the gods, mantras and Veda to what ripens from it.

The Kural asks what learning has achieved if it does not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge, so bowing is learning's fruit. Tirumular bows by leaving what he learned (கற்றன விட்டேன்): the feet are reached by setting learning down.
Both set a true lamp above ordinary lamps. For the Kural it is truthfulness; for Tirumular it is the lamp that lights the lamp, and its bearer becomes the lamp.
725 tells how Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Highest had made it his temple and so guards it; 1823 maps the temple onto the body part by part.

The Naladiyar calls the body a pot seeping filth from nine openings, dressed in skin that fools the eye; Tirumular makes the same flesh body (ஊனுடம்பு) the Lord's shrine and the mouth its gate. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar is read as judging the body's worth itself, not only rebuking lust.

The Kural says water gives outer purity and truth inner purity. Tirumular makes truthful speech and thought the condition without which the Lord is not seen, and only then counts flowers and water as praise.
Both say worship needs almost nothing: 252 offers the Lord one green leaf, open to anyone; 1828 says flowers and water are always there, so those who fail to approach are evading.

Both redirect offering from the Lord's image to his living devotees: 1857 says what is given to the walking temple reaches the Lord, 1829 that the water washing a jnani's feet is the Lord's bath in the nine holy waters.
Both make the sea of births what drowns those who do not turn to the Lord: the Kural's who do not reach his feet cannot swim it, Tirumular's who do not worship sink (அழுந்துகின்றார்) in it.
The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and the rest is noisy show; Tirumular says daily adorning and praise do not bring knowledge of the Lord until the inner stain is gone.
1852 says worship belongs where moon and sun do not shine; 1853 says what moon and sun become there, bindu and nada, and where the worship is done.
1855 says the Lord takes the worship not done by day and night; 1856 speaks from that place, where night and day are not and the worship is drinking bliss.
1823 makes the body a temple and the soul a Siva-linga; 1857 draws the consequence for giving: the devotee is a walking temple, and what he receives reaches the god of the built one.
Both rank feeding a jnani above the great religious gifts; 1851 by multiples of merit, 1860 against a thousand villages and a thousand temple towers.
Both set one simple act above a thousand great rites: the Kural puts not killing and eating above a thousand sacrifices, Tirumular puts one meal for a jnani above a thousand gifts to Brahmins.
The Kural sees householders as those who provide for renunciants, perhaps at the cost of their own austerity; Tirumular makes that provision the highest merit, above feeding Brahmins.
1858 says what the ascetic eats the three worlds eat; 1866 says the three gods eat it, and adds that his leavings give release.
Both say the land where a devotee lives is blessed: 1868 with peace and rain, 1882 with true knowers and good order, and release from births.
The Kural makes giving and austerity depend on rain; Tirumular runs it the other way, making rain depend on the presence of one who seeks the Lord.
audit_text_issue: 1868's ஒரு வாது இருக்கில் is probably a corruption of ஒருவன் இருக்கில்

note: Both speak of Tirumular as bound and sent by the Lord: 1863 as Nandi's message, 1876 by a deed of servitude written before birth.
Both place the Lord in the devotee: 1857 tells the giver that food for the walking temple reaches the god, 1885 tells the devotee that he begs and eats for the Lord in the temple within.

Both put the world's creator beside begging. The Kural says that if the maker of the world decreed that people live by begging he should wander and perish; Tirumular says the maker of the seven worlds begged himself so that his devotees could reach him by begging. The conflict holds if the Kural is read as condemning all living by alms, not only the beggary of the poor.

Both fault begging that comes from desire when the remedy lies within: the Naladiyar asks why one should beg of strangers when poverty can be ended by asking of oneself, Tirumular faults those who beg for their desires instead of reaping the field already ploughed.
The Kural says pain ends when desire, anger and confusion are gone; Tirumular says hunger, craving and anger do not stay in Siva's devotees, and adds that they pass beyond the heavens too.
audit_text_issue: kural:360: இநவ்முன்றன் is corrupt; read இவ்மூன்றன்.

note: Both use வர இருந்தான் (waiting so as to come or be come to): in 1889 the Lord waits on the way, in 1891 the ascetic waits and the world comes to him.
1893 names shambhavi and khechari among the mudras; 1894 says what each one is: the Lord's glance, and the truth that rises with Om.
Both put the mudra of silence highest: 1895 calls it release beyond release, 1900 the seal of the liberated.
The Kural says whatever else one fails to guard, one should guard the tongue; Tirumular says guarding the tongue alone only makes one mute, and silence is true only when the mind is still too.
audit_text_issue: Line 4 has the typo சுத்த்ததை for சுத்தத்தை.

note: The Siva-yogi of 1905 goes to a higher world and comes back; the faultless jnani of 1906 does not return. Together they rank the yogi below the jnani in what death brings.

Both make release a matter of not coming back: the Kural's மற்றீண்டு வாரா நெறி and Tirumular's மீளார். Tirumular adds the setting of a silent samadhi at death; the Kural says only that seeing the true thing here leads there.

Both speak of what is done with a corpse once its life has left. The Naladiyar asks what it matters whether it is dragged off, buried or thrown anywhere; Tirumular says that burning or exposing a jnani's body ruins the land. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar's indifference covers every body; if it speaks only of ordinary people, Tirumular's exception for the jnani escapes it.

Both tie the failure of rain to a wrong: in the Kural a king's crooked rule, in Tirumular the burning of a jnani's body. The same belief that the sky answers moral or sacred offence is applied to kingship and to the rites of the dead.
1823 makes the body of flesh a temple of the Lord; 1911 draws the consequence for the jnani's corpse: to burn it is to set fire to the Lord's temple.

The chapter's two bindus: the cosmic one from which kundalini, gods and speech unfold (1923), and the drop distilled from food in the body (1934). Tirumular gives both the same name and the same generative role.
audit_text_issue: 1923's last line (கலைவை கரியே) is compressed or corrupt

note: 1931 says the Lord is in the seed unperceived; 1932 states the logic: no sprout apart from its seed, and seed and sprout only together.

Both use dew on a grass blade. The Naladiyar makes it the body's brief life and urges good deeds now; Tirumular makes it the rare drop of bindu from which the body's strength grows, something to be kept rather than a reminder of loss.
724 says that if the body perishes the life perishes, and that Tirumular learned how to nourish the body; 1936 names one way it perishes, the unguarded loss of bindu.

Both start from the perishing body. The Naladiyar's wise see it as a bubble and resolve to end their births; Tirumular faults people for not guarding what keeps the body. The facts agree, the response differs.
1936 laments that people do not know how bindu is lost or how to guard it; 1948 lists what stays when it is kept: breath, strength, intellect, tapas, japa, silence and siddhi.

Both give the same sequence: kindle the fire at the root, raise it through the sealed central way, and drink the nectar. 1949 calls those who do it Siva-yogis; 1962 calls it bindu's victory by Shakti.
1946 says there is no harvest except for the sower; 1964 turns this into a riddle of three men who pound, roast or sow the seed, and only the sower is apart.
1933 traces food into body and mind, and 1934 into bindu; 1966 names the bindu of food and the bindu of breath and makes knowing both the way to the golden body.
1923 makes cosmic bindu the source of powers, gods and speech; 1969 makes bindu and nada the source of all lives and mantras, and then turns to the bodily bindu whose containment brings Sivoham.
Both see woman as கூற்று, Death. In the Kural the lover discovers it, struck by her eyes; Tirumular makes it a deliberate meditation that ends desire and with it death.

The Naladiyar quells desire by taking the woman's body apart into entrails and blood. Tirumular does not reject union: kept with bindu unspent, it is Siva's own pleasure, and only the fool's infatuation is condemned.
Both open on the sun's hidden road under the earth (பகலோன் வரும்வழி) and say no one knows it; 1984 adds what the learned say, that it circles the mountain, and that those who know the town know.

1981 says the world's divided talk babbles and passes while the truth in the light goes unseen; 1986, in the body's sun, says those who find where the sun settles still all that babble with it. Same words, பேதித்து and பிதற்று.

Both put the decisive event in the குழல்வழி, the tube or central channel: in 754 the Dancer stands there for those who see the feet, in 1985 a victorious light shines there once the malams are killed.

note: 1923 lists what comes from bindu; 1993 divides bindu into lower and higher and pictures the unfolding as a dawn in the heart, setting up the chapter's sun of knowledge.
audit_text_issue: 1923's last line (கலைவை கரியே) looks compressed or corrupt

note: 2002 says Siva is in each body like the sun in many pots, not shut in by them; 2010 says he is in the soul and the soul in him, while being everywhere. Presence within without confinement, in two images.
2006 has the two swans that never part and faults the swan that holds itself apart; 2017 says there is no difference of soul and Siva once Siva is known. Both deny the soul a separate standing.
Both measure subtlety by repeated division: 2008 divides the atom into a thousand to reach the Lord in it, 2011 divides a cow's hair into a hundred and then a thousand to give the soul's size.
Both picture the senses as fields where animals graze: 2016 has cows that must be led past the boundary, 2025 birds feeding in five fields and a herdsman with a staff.
1924 counts the thirty-six tattvas; 2020 says the count is learned from Nandi by grace and is the step to standing beyond them.
audit_text_issue: 1924's numbers (25 + 6 + two twos) do not sum to 36 as read; a number may be lost.

note: Both judge outward ascetic marks worthless without inner change: the Kural says neither shaving nor matted hair is needed if one gives up what is condemned (Parimelazhagar counts hair-plucking under shaving); Tirumular says hair-tearers do not know the impurities or grace.

Both picture the senses as five elephants to be controlled. The Kural says the one who guards them with the goad of firmness is a seed for release; Tirumular shows the mahout exhausted and confesses he does not know how to manage it. The goal agrees; the confidence that it can be done does not.
Two animal images for the same discipline: the Kural's tortoise draws its five limbs in; Tirumular's five lions go out to feed and must have claws and teeth cut. Withdrawal against disarming.

Both count five senses and the gates through which craving comes and goes, and make guarding them the way to release; the Naladiyar names the five gates, Tirumular adds the nine openings and a herdsman.
2024 shows a mahout who cannot steer the leaping beast; in 2028 the poet says he himself has become that unruly horse.

The Kural asks what is stronger than fate; Tirumular gives fate's great strength the earth but assigns heaven to praise and human life to the mind, so fate is one power among several. The tension depends on reading 2030's domains as limits.

The Kural says the field of the five must be crushed (அடல்வேண்டும்); Tirumular calls those who say 'curb the five' ignorant and says full curbing makes one inert. The conflict holds if 2033 is read as rejecting suppression of the senses, as its wording says, rather than only a wrong method of it.
The same chapter that mocks curbing the five (அடக்கு) praises subsiding in the five (ஒடுங்கு) as tapas and Hara's state: the objection is to forcing the senses, not to their stilling.

Both treat the five senses as elephants to be held, the Kural's guarded by the goad of firmness (on Parimelazhagar's reading), Tirumular's by a fort of knowledge. In the Kural the guard works; in Tirumular the elephants break out.
In 977 the five elephants of the forest are held by the goad of the five letters; in 2034 a fort of knowledge fails to hold them. Mantra succeeds where bare knowledge did not.
Both make mastery of the five a supreme power: the Kural calls Indra witness to it, Tirumular calls it the wide world, tapas and Hara's state.
Both count life away by its units of time, the Kural's day a saw cutting life, Tirumular's nazhigais and days already gone; Tirumular draws the lesson of conquering the senses now.
Both end with blind and blind falling into the pit; 1680 blames the pupils who choose a guru who cannot cure blindness, 2048 the blind guru who shows the stick.
Both define the Siva-guru by the same act, showing the real, the unreal and the real-unreal (சத்தும் அசத்தும் சதசத்தும்).

Both use transmutation by contact: whatever comes to the golden mountain takes its colour (1511), whatever the philosopher's stone touches becomes gold (2054); both make the guru's presence change the one who comes near.
2051 says the iron once turned to gold never turns back; 2054 names the agent, the guru as a touchstone, and widens it to all the world he touches.
Both make the guru's path the one road that Nandi set out for salvation.

Both deny that hidden wrong is hidden: in the Kural the five elements within laugh at the deceiver's concealed conduct, in Tirumular the Lord stands everywhere as overseer. The Kural's witness is in the body, Tirumular's is the Lord.
2039 makes north and south the temple of the mind; 2070 says the world gathered in the north is within, against those who walk north to find it.
1729 says Nandi took the body as his temple; 2071 faults those who search the land for the one fragrant within the body.
Both end in களவொழிந்தாரே; 2067 says stealth ends when the overseer is seen, 2074 says how he is seen: not with the eye, whose film hides the light.
Both ask what is gained by learning or argument that does not end in bowing at the Lord's feet; Tirumular names disputation (வாது) where the Kural names learning.
The Kural says only those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births; Tirumular laments those who, given a rare human birth, never cherish those feet and so lose what that birth was for.
Both press for action before death arrives: the Kural before the hiccup stops the tongue, Tirumular while the porridge still boils and death runs near.

Both deny that birth ranks people: the Kural says birth is alike for all and distinction comes from deeds; Tirumular says kin is one and God is one. The Kural keeps a distinction by deeds that Tirumular does not mention.
1581 says Nandi taught that the guru is Siva; 2120 adds the condition, a guru who is a flawless knower, and says such a one is to be called nothing but the Supreme.
Both make reaching the Lord the end of births: the Kural's crossing of the sea of births, Tirumular's freedom from all birth for the soul that holds the Lord in mind at death.

Both make the body a bag left behind when its occupant goes: in 167 the dancer leaves the leather bag, so what crows do to it no longer matters; in 2122 the thief leaves and the maya-bag turns to earth.
2124 repeats 473 almost word for word; in the chapter on conception it describes the forming embryo, here the subtle body of eight.

Both list the body's stuffs, fat, blood, bone, flesh, skin. The Naladiyar asks which of these is the beloved, to cure desire; Tirumular names them as the gross adjunct beneath the subtle bodies, without disgust.
494 names the classes of soul (விஞ்ஞானர், எஞ்ஞானர், மெய்ஞ்ஞானர்) by the malas they have left; 2136 gives each its body: anava, maya, karma, or Siva.
725 says Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Lord's temple within it and now tends it; 2137 calls those who dismiss the body as filth dull.

The Naladiyar says the great saw the body's foulness and abandoned it; Tirumular calls those who disregard the body as filth dull and finds the cosmos in it. The conflict holds if மலம் in 2137 is read as bodily filth, as here.

The Kural calls virtue the companion that does not perish when one perishes; Tirumular says vows and gifts are no sure support for the perishing flesh. The two can agree if the Kural speaks of the person and Tirumular of the body; the verse does not settle which it means.
Both picture the body as a king's realm with horses and a company of five: in 2147 as the arrayed camp of the waking instruments, in 2165 as a city whose five servants sleep when the king rides in.
2142 places dream at the throat with fourteen instruments; 2154 says which ten fall away and that dream is built from the impressions of household life.
2162 describes anava as a stupor from which the soul falls into the states; 2163 gives the Lord's side: the states are his waking of the sleeper through maya.
2160 says the five malas keep every soul in endless birth and death; 2166 says the same five, seen plainly in waking, are the way to stand with the Supreme.
Tirumular takes the Kural's own phrase, உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை நட்பு. The Kural says that bond ends as a bird leaves its shell; Tirumular faults people who never come to know it.
Both separate the life from the body it lives in: the Naladiyar's dancer leaves the skin bag, and Tirumular's fools cling to bodies without knowing the life inside.
Both use the tortoise drawing in for the five senses held in. In the Kural it is self-restraint that guards through seven births; in Tirumular it follows when the silent and spoken letters meet.
audit_text_issue: tm:2158 begins with a stray 'Y' before ஊமை.

note: Both treat birth as a waking from sleep. The Kural uses it to show how quickly birth and death alternate; Tirumular makes embodiment the Lord's waking of the soul from anava's deeper sleep.
Both reach the Vedanta count of twenty-eight from the twenty-four, but add different items to it: 2172 purusha, the Supreme and the void, 2176 turiya, inner time, the void and the higher turiya.
2178 reduces the countless tattvas to ninety-six and twenty-five; 2179 says which school counts which, making ninety-six common and thirty-six the Saiva count.
2170 pictures one who sits in the web of the senses and consumes their objects; 2181 separates the knower from all thirty-six inert tattvas, a knowledge the soul gets only from Nandi.
Both make the letter A stand for what is first: the Kural compares God's place in the world to A among letters, and Tirumular names the real tattva the letter A.
2160 says the five malas bind every soul; 2183 grades them by the rank of beings, from five in the lowest to anava alone in Sadasiva.
2182 removes the five states, the five mala-states and the false thirty-six so that the soul stands as one; 2186 names where that ends, in the dance and in becoming Siva, with the five made Sivaya.

A near-repetition: both place waking, dream, deep sleep and turiya at the brow, throat, heart and navel with fewer instruments in each. They differ in the counts (ஐஐந்தில் against பன்னான்கில்) and in the third line (பொய்கண்ட மூவர் against பொய்கண்டிலாத புருடன்), which may show a corrupt copy in one or both.
audit_text_issue: counts (ஐஐந்தில் vs பன்னான்கில்) and line 3 differ; one or both may be corrupt

note: Both use பசு in its double sense of cattle and bound soul. 2015 sorts the cows by what they yield, only the mature ones giving milk; 2193 makes them all one in their milk and one in their herdsman.
2192 names the three malas and calls for separating the soul from them; 2211 says the Lord gave the tattvas and instruments for exactly that, so that the malas might be cut.

Both make release the end of an obscuring mixture: the Kural's stainless sight, freed from confusion, removes darkness and brings joy; Tirumular says Shakti, knowledge and Siva are hidden by mala and light appears when the mixture ends. Tirumular names what hides; the Kural names only confusion.
Both trace a bad end to delusion: the Kural's confusion that takes the unreal as real yields a joyless birth, and in 2194 the soul whose delusion grows reaches the seven hells.

The Kural guards the five senses with the elephant goad of firmness; Tirumular ends his verse on standing in the true way before the mind scatters with a charging elephant. The pairing holds if 2215's elephant is the mastered senses or mind; if it is the strength one gains, the images only touch.
2209 says that after knowing the knowledge that knows, one becomes that knower; 2224 turns this into a riddle: who can know the knower who knows without knowing?
audit_text_issue: TM 2224 அறியாதவத்தை may divide two ways.

note: Both say a person is the maker of his own rise and fall: the Naladiyar names who sets a man up and casts him down and answers 'himself', Tirumular says he is his own enemy, friend, next world and master.
The Kural traces joyless birth to taking the unreal for the real; Tirumular's first error is the same kind, taking the body for the self, and it too ends in birth again.
2014 has the soul enter turiya and become knowledge; 2264 adds that turiya not joined to the Lord still leads back to birth.
Near-repetition: both open with the two deeds balancing and grace-power coming as or through the guru, and end with the impurities removed, as becoming Siva in 1527 and as non-birth here.
audit_text_issue: 2262 இருவிடை is evidently a slip for இருவினை.

note: 1924's numbers for the thirty-six tattvas do not add up as read; 2267 gives the standard grouping clearly, twenty-four impure, seven pure-impure and five pure.
audit_text_issue: 1924's counts (ஐ ஐந்து, ஆறு, ஈரிரண்டு) do not sum to ஆறுஆறு; a number may be corrupt

note: Paired images of mutual concealment: gold and ornament for the soul and its faculties, wood and carved elephant for the Lord and the elements.
2288 makes knowing oneself the way to know the Lord; 2279 adds that knowing oneself alone doesn't end birth unless one knows the pervading Lord.
Both play on பற்று: the Kural bids one cling to the one without clinging in order to let go, Tirumular says the Supreme is grasped as attachment ends.
Both place the giving up of anger where one has the power to act on it: the Kural says restraint counts only where anger can take effect, Tirumular says let it go while you can still win.

note: Both use the tortoise drawing in its five. The Kural makes restraint of the senses in one birth a shelter through seven; Tirumular puts the tortoise in a silent well and promises it a thousand years if it withdraws into truth.

Both treat the five senses as elephants to be mastered (in the Kural through the goad of firmness, as Parimelazhagar reads it). The Kural's reward is the field of release; Tirumular adds a lamp of knowledge lit inside the body.
The Kural defines understanding as seeing the true thing in whatever thing appears; Tirumular narrows it to knowing oneself, and calls every other knowing a ghoul's.
251 says those who know themselves bow to the Lord and find him kin; 2318 says such self-knowing is the only knowledge that counts.
2323 has Nandi tell the soul it is the knower; 2329 adds that the soul does not know by itself and knows only when grace illumines it.
Both use fire and its heat. In 2309 the heat left in iron after the fire is gone is karma's residue; in 2341 heat inseparable from fire is grace inseparable from the Lord.

417 makes the Lord the potter who shapes pots and births; 2351 likens him instead to the one clay in all vessels, and to the eye that sees all but itself. The two images give maker and inner presence.
1512 defines Saivam as knowing oneself and reaching Siva; 2355 opens the chapter on knowledge with the same claim from the other side: not to know oneself is ruin.
2355 states the rule that knowing oneself brings no harm; 2366 tells it as the speaker's own history, from long not knowing to a knowing after which nothing else is known.

The Kural sets understanding against the folly (பேதைமை) that is birth. Tirumular says the knowledge that frees lies beyond both the world's knowledge and its ignorance, so the line falls not between them but past them.
Both make understanding a kind of total possession: the Kural says those with it have everything, Tirumular that their heart is the wide world itself and the place where the first Lord stays.
1449 mentions the six of wide Vedanta and Siddhanta without listing them, if மாறும் is read as ஆறும்; 2370 names the six ends, Vedanta and Siddhanta first.
2381 turns the ends into the triad of knowing, known and knower; 2382 then dissolves the triad itself, ends into known, knower into known, knowledge gone, leaving silence and bliss.
Both make silence a mudra, a seal: 1900 calls the seal of silence the mark of the liberated, and 2386 ends the unity of Vedanta and Siddhanta in sinking into the silence of the seal.

1509 ends the grades of release when the bond dissolves and the Lord is sayujya; 2392 reads tat tvam asi onto the same scheme: 'thou' is the soul, 'that' the Lord left when the bond goes, and their union sayujya.
1435 calls Siddhanta not other than Vedanta; 2393 says both are the one aim of becoming Siva, each in vain apart from it.
2399 counts the ends as five, not six; 2400 holds the five together with Vedanta and Siddhanta made one, which explains the count.
audit_text_issue: TM 2400 அன்னை after ஐவகைஅந்தம் may be corrupt.

note: Both make the Veda and the Agama the Lord's own speech and, read rightly, the source of one Vedanta-Siddhanta; 2397 adds that the Veda is general and the Agama special.
2017 says soul and Siva are not different and that souls who know Siva remain as Siva; 2402 calls that knowing of soul and Siva the meaning of tat tvam asi.
Both call what true knowledge reaches செம்பொருள், the perfect thing, and tie it to release. The Kural leaves it unnamed; Tirumular says Siddhanta and Vedanta are that perfect meaning and show Siva.

note: 2411 calls the bond the good bond, the altar before the lingam; 2422 explains why it is good: like dirt put on cloth to clean it, the bond is grace's instrument.
Both name the Lord as the one who performs the five acts (ஐங்கருமம்) through bindu; 1927 calls him the seed and root, 2416 places the acts in the subtle order of bindu and nada.
The Kural asks for cutting the pride that says 'I' and 'mine'; Tirumular names that 'I'-saying as anava, the root bond itself, and adds that grace is the means of its removal.
Both join the Lord's feet to the head. The Kural calls a head that does not bow to them useless; in Tirumular the feet come down onto the head, as grace given rather than worship offered.
2427 says Nandi's feet came onto the poet's head; 2433 says what they did there: cut his bonds and his delusion and took him.
2421 makes grace the means to reach the Lord's feet; 2425 makes the feet themselves grace, which shows the soul knowledge.
audit_text_issue: 2425 line 3 (பாலொன்று ஞானமே பண்பார் தலைஉயிர்) is hard to divide

note: Tirumular takes the Kural's three, காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம், word for word. The Kural says that when their very names perish, suffering perishes; Tirumular says that with them driven out he reached the abode within Om.
2425 makes the Lord's foot Shakti as grace, which brings the soul to knowledge; 2439 makes 'art', the word that joins soul and Lord, the station of Shakti.
2443 has the Lord setting going waking and the other states; 2444 places them inside the supreme turiya and names its rare turiya as the joining word.

Both turn on பற்று: the Kural bids one cling to the one without clinging in order to let go of clinging; Tirumular repeats 'clinging so that clinging ends' in every line and makes it the way to the supreme beyond the supreme.

Both use the cow and her calf. In the Naladiyar the calf finds its mother among many cows as an old deed finds its doer; in Tirumular the mother rises at the thought of her calf, as the Lord comes to the soul. One image carries karma, the other grace.
Both end on a lamp on a hill: in 2407 worship makes the knowledge like a lamp on the western hill, in 2446 Nandi becomes a lamp of virtue filling the hill.
Both have the freed soul passing through kevala to the state beyond while still in waking (நனவில் அதீதம்).
2456 says Nandi cut away the tattvas, the two mayas and fear; 2457 adds what followed: he led the speaker beyond knowing and gave himself.
Both make Shakti the Supreme's body or form: in 2459 as his body moving in will and knowledge, in 2464 as the open space within the five elements.
Both use the crystal that shows what is near it. The Kural makes it the face showing the mind; Tirumular makes it the soul taking the colour of the Supreme it comes within.
2466 matches the three turiyas with the three padas; 2488 restates it as soul, Supreme and Siva appearing in turiya as tvam tat asi.
Both name the goal செம்பொருள். For the Kural, seeing it is the work of knowledge that ends birth; for Tirumular, Nandi as the true reality takes him and gives it by grace.
Both trace birth to not knowing what truly is: the Kural to the delusion that takes the unreal as real, Tirumular to souls that do not know what is. Tirumular adds that those who know come to grace.
Both use a gem whose light, lustre and rays belong to it: 2482 for the three forms resting in the Lord, 2483 for the experience in the three voids.
audit_text_issue: 2483's நாடிஒண் முப்பதும் and முத்திராந்தத்து are obscure, possibly corrupt

note: Both argue identity through one man seen differently: 2485 one man in three roles, 2493 Devadatta recognised as the same man once changed circumstances are set aside.
Both name a set of three whose ending ends the trouble: the Kural desire, anger and delusion, whose very names must perish; Tirumular the impurities and qualities, whose dying lets Siva appear.
audit_text_issue: Kural 360 reads இநவ்முன்றன் for இம்மூன்றன்; 2489 காமதம் is doubtful.

note: 2497 ends at rest in a void beyond imagining; 2500 says that for those who know, there is no void either, nor heart nor form.
2503 maps the letters சி, வா, ய to Siva, the Supreme and the soul; 2499 drops நம to leave those letters as the clear form of the mantra.
2495 lets go the seven effects and seven causes to reach the voids; 2505 says the bound soul mixes in the seven effects and Parasiva in the seven causes, and the Supreme is in the void beyond both.
Both say the Supreme too has adjuncts: 2463 that even the Supreme clinging to a causal adjunct is not pure, 2501 that the seven adjuncts of the Supreme must be cut away with the soul's.
Both speak of a sea to be crossed. The Kural's sea is births, swum only by those at the Lord's feet; Tirumular's knower has already seen the shore, the waves of the soul settled to clear water.
The Kural defines folly as the conceit 'we are wise'; Tirumular's heartless men say 'we know fully' while blind to the Lord, as futile as cutting the hare from the moon.

Both name the pride of 'I' and 'mine' as what must be cut. The Kural promises a world beyond the gods' to the one who cuts it; Tirumular makes cutting it, with the lesser releases set aside, the mark of the Siva-siddha.
Both make mastering the five senses the condition of reaching the Lord: the Kural's one who quenched the five senses, Tirumular's one who conquers them and knows him as one.
2530 names a river and an inner tank; 2535 places the tank on a hilltop, filled without a river, and adds the lotus without mud worn by Siva.
Both set standing and sitting and many words against the one who conquers and seeks the Lord: talk and posture do not reach him, mastery does.
2537 only names the nine presiding selves; 2545 sets them in the nine states and makes passing beyond their three turiyas into Siva the goal.
The same verse appears word for word as 2071; the repetition places the search for Nandi within the body under the heading of purity as well.
725 tells how Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Lord's temple within it and began to tend it; 2550 faults those who search the land for the Lord fragrant within the body.

Both say people do not know what the body is. For the Naladiyar its truth is the stinking cart the vultures tear when life leaves it; for Tirumular it holds Nandi, fragrant within. The tension holds if the Naladiyar's verse is read as a judgement of the body itself, not only of vanity about adorning it.

The Kural sets outer purity by water against inner purity by truthfulness; Tirumular also moves purity inward but keeps ritual among its sources: discipline, worship, the fire rite and knowledge free one from ritual impurity.
Both fix a place by finger-breadths from the nose: 581 twelve below it, as a point of meditation that keeps the body; 2546 three or four from its tip, as the Lord's unknown dwelling.
Both set the Real (பொருள்) against delusion (மருள்): the Kural makes taking the unreal for the real the cause of base births; Tirumular leaves all but the Lord's devotees whirling in delusion.

2566 names the third mode, implication that leaves and keeps (விட்டுவிடாத இலக்கணை); 2570 applies it to the great saying, as in the Vedantic example 'this is that Devadatta', to make the soul the Supreme.
2568 sets out the saying analytically, word by word and turiya by turiya; 2577 says what completes it: 'you are that' must become 'I have become that', and this happens by Nandi's grace.

2580 tells the seeker to put away both knowing and not-knowing before Siva who is knowledge itself; 2581 gives the reason: the soul knows the elements, but knows the Lord only as the Lord makes it know.
Both see the body as a bubble. The Naladiyar's wise draw from it the resolve to end their births; Tirumular sets the bubble beside camphor in fire and has the body go into the Supreme.
2590 says the Supreme eats the world and spits it out again; 2593 says what is swallowed, soul, Supreme, turiya and the cosmos, and that it stays outwardly whole like the emptied wood-apple.

The Kural says one who is not false in his heart dwells in the hearts of all people; Tirumular says the Lord dwells with those mingled in truth and does not enter before the false. Truthfulness opens the heart in both: to others in the Kural, to the Lord in Tirumular.
The Kural says knowledge from the five senses is no gain without true perception; Tirumular says knowing everything is no gain apart from the knowledge that knows everything.

Both deny that knowledge profits by itself: the Kural asks what learning gains without worship of the one of pure knowledge, Tirumular says knowing all things gains nothing apart from the all-knowing.

Both make the way out of bondage a following: the Kural says cling to the one without clinging in order to let clinging go, Tirumular says cut the senses' bond and follow the one who cut away confusion.
The Kural praises those who keep to the path of the one who quenched the five senses; Tirumular tells the seeker to cut the five senses' bond and follow the one who has done so.
2610 says how the jnani deals with former and later karma; 2611 says by what power: Siva's grace placed on the head.

note: Both have the wise meet arriving karma calmly: the Naladiyar's wise take it as old debt and are freed of confusion, Tirumular's jnanis live it out and are rid of it.

The Kural says nothing is stronger than what is apportioned, which arrives before any scheme to avoid it. Tirumular grants that former karma must be lived out, but adds that the jnani can stop karma not yet made, which the Kural's verse does not address.

note: Both free the Lord's own from the hold of deeds: in the Kural the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who praise him, in Tirumular the jnani unties former karma by Siva's grace.
Both make cutting desire the one test that counts: the Kural says only those free of desire are truly free, Tirumular says yogic talk of breath is useless until desire and attachment are cut.

In verse 298 Tirumular says if you cling, cling to the Supreme; here he says cut desire even if it is for the Lord. The conflict holds if ஆசை here is the same as பற்று there; if 2615 means desire for gains from the Lord, the two fit.

The Kural tells the renouncer to cling to the one free of clinging as the means of letting go; Tirumular tells him to cut desire even for the Lord. It depends on reading ஈசனோடாயினும் as desire directed at the Lord himself.
Both say desire is the source of sorrow and its ending brings unbroken joy: the Kural calls desire the sorrow of sorrows, Tirumular says bliss grows as desire is let go.
Both tie release to mastering the longing (வேட்கை) that works through the five: the Naladiyar has it guarded at the five gates of the senses, Tirumular has it flung away with the five elements.

note: Both set அவா (desire) beside தவா (unfailing): the Kural calls desire the seed of unfailing births, Tirumular has humans sunk in the sea of desire while the Lord holds the unfailing sea.
Both deny the Lord a dwelling outside the person: 2614 says he is in no mansion, hall or temple but in the desireless heart, 2650 says this one's house is his only house.

2615 says cut desire even for the Lord; here the creeper reaches the Lord joined with longing (விருப்பொடு கூடி). Read together, longing that seeks the Lord is not the desire 2615 cuts, unless 2640's longing belongs to Uma alone.

note: 2614 says the Lord is in no temple but in the desireless heart; 2641 tells it as experience: Nandi comes and takes the inner self as his temple.

2940, in the chapter on the samadhi of silence, opens with the same line, the light shining beyond the three turiyas, and also speaks of expanding and contracting; here the state is the guru's and cannot be spoken, there it is a state of experience beyond speech.

The Kural calls a head that does not bow to the Lord's feet as useless as a sense that cannot perceive; Tirumular says the same from the other side, that his head, mouth, eyes and mind were given to him for Nandi.

Both make the small great by what they cling to: in the Naladiyar the hare is worshipped with the moon it lives in, so the slight gain worth by friendship with steady men; in Tirumular those as small as a split millet seed become high by reaching the Lord with a firm mind.

The Kural makes one's own deeds the touchstone of greatness and smallness; Tirumular names another measure, the mind that reaches the Lord, by which even the smallest become high. The two need not conflict, but the test differs.

2664 says that one who stands in the sixteen-fold path (சோடச மார்க்கம்) sees as other what seemed oneself; 2680 places the same path among the sanmargis and names the stages they pass beyond to rest at the end of knowing.

note: 2677 makes Om the source of elements, world and souls; 2699, on the five letters, takes Om apart as A, U and M and turns from it to Na, the first letter of Nandi's name.
Both give Siva three eyes that are three lights: here sun, moon and the forehead fire, in 2774 the three eyes in the dancer's body whose limbs are space and the eight directions.

Both use light driving out darkness: in the Naladiyar austerity drives out sin as a lamp does darkness, and evil returns when good deeds run out like a lamp's oil; in Tirumular the Lord's light casts off maya's darkness through renunciation, with no word of its return.

965, in the chapter on the chakra of the holy hall, is nearly the same verse; there the fifty letters 'go' and become the five (எழுத்தும்போய்), here they simply are the five. The repetition ties the five letters of this chapter to the earlier letter diagrams.

Both begin from the letter A as the first of all letters. The Kural uses it as a simile for the Lord as first of the world; Tirumular traces the letters from A through Om to Na, the first letter of Nandi's name, so the alphabet itself leads to the Lord.
2094 tells people to worship the Lord daily until they sleep (துஞ்சும் அளவும்); 2707 gives the words for that hour, calling him Lord and his feet refuge.

2704 says that saying Sivaya nama makes nectar well up; 2709, opening the next chapter, makes the same formula an alchemical pill that turns the body to gold. Both give the recited name a bodily effect.
Both make the five letters an alchemy: chanting turns copper to gold in 905, and in 2709 the mantra is a குளிகை that turns the body to gold, which makes the body the metal transformed.
Both drop நம from the mantra as the soul's bound part: 1013 calls it the soul and says when it falls away the search ends, 2712 calls it impurity and leaves சிவாய as the truth free of it.

979 says சிவாய becomes the soul, its enjoyment and knowledge and ends in becoming Siva; 2711 spells out what the full name holds (Siva, grace, soul, concealment, impurity) and how the last are stilled before the soul becomes the supreme Siva.

Both free a person from deeds through the Lord's name: the Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who love his true praise, Tirumular that saying Siva Siva makes evil deeds die. Tirumular adds the converse, that evil-doers do not say it.

Both answer endless learning with a choice: the Naladiyar says learning has no shore and life is short, so take only what is fitting, as the swan takes milk from water; Tirumular names the one thing to take, the Lord's letter, and makes it the vessel that does reach the shore.

Both picture release as crossing to a shore: the Kural's great sea of births is crossed only by those who reach the Lord's feet, and in 2720 the one who masters the Lord's letter is a vessel that has reached the farther shore.

The Kural calls letters and numbers the two eyes of the living; 2721 calls those who boast of knowing letters fools, because they don't know the letter that masters letters. The difference rests on எழுத்து meaning script in the Kural and the mantra in Tirumular, so it qualifies rather than contradicts.

Both use liquor to measure an intoxication that comes without drinking. The Kural says brewed liquor delights only those who drink it, while love delights those who merely see; Tirumular says the frenzy of Siva's bliss comes to those who saw the dance and even to those who only heard of it.

Both put a dancer inside the body. The Naladiyar's dancer is the soul in its skin bag, and once it leaves, the body does not matter; Tirumular's dancers in every embodied life are Siva and Shakti themselves.

The Kural says only those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births; Tirumular uses the same 'reaching the feet' to define the devotee, and makes the feet those of the dancer seen in the golden hall.
1726 says the human body's form is Chidambaram and the holy dance; 2770 locates the small hall at one point in it, the space between the brows reached by fixed gaze.
919 says the five letters are seated as the temple; 2775 says the hall of the dance is the five letters. Both make the mantra the shrine.

Two verses of nearly the same shape: the dancing foot, the sound that rises with it and the songs, and then 'this is how I saw'. 2317 sees them within the nadi; 2760 sees them within at the guru's word and ends the search there.
2727 says the five dances are the five acts; 2799 assigns each act to a part of the dancer: drum, hand, fire and the two feet.
Both map the body's three channels onto the land, with Meru and Tillai as the central channel and the Himalaya and Lanka at the sides; 2754 states the matching more plainly.
2797 reads the dancer's hands as syllables; 2798 adds the foot and tells the reader to recite சிவாயநம in that form.
The same four-line pattern: what the ignorant say, that no one knows the dance, and what the dance is once known. In 2787 it is the Shakti of grace; in 2796 it is the end of the self.
2778 says seeing the dance works as the sight of tamarind does on the mouth; 2779 extends the effect from seeing to hearing.

2685 ranks the lights of the five elements, with space among them, and gathers all five into one; 2812 takes space alone and grades it from the outer worlds to the knowing within and the light in Siva.
audit_text_issue: Both verses are obscure; 2685's order is unclear.

note: Both verses are built on repeated விளக்கு (lamp): in 1818 lighting the lamp lets one know the open space and those who light it shine in it; in 2816 the lamp lit within the lamp leads to the feet of the lamp's owner.
2815 names the churning, Siva taking the poison so the gods could drink nectar; 2823 turns that nectar into what Siva himself is to those who can see.

In 2592 the Lord takes the poet into himself like water into hot iron and swallows the light of the three voids; 2825 describes the bliss of one who has gone past the three voids into supreme knowledge-bliss.
2437 names the three padas, 'thou', 'that' and 'art', which bring one to Siva; 2826 gives each its turiya and puts the good in the third.

The water lily (உற்பலம்) whose form, colour, scent and beauty cannot be separated: in 2829 for truth and the rest in the soul's union, in 2843 for the guru in whom form and quality are swallowed into the true form.
2820 says the Lord granted that 'I' and 'He' are not two and the poet's thinking ceased; 2846 speaks from the far side of that gift: the First can now be called 'I'.

Both ground equanimity in fate: the Kural asks why those who accept good fortune grieve at bad; Tirumular's knowers are unchanged whether anointed with sandal or struck with a chisel, since all comes by Nandi's decree.

The Kural says one enjoys only as the apportioner (வகுத்தான்) apportioned; Tirumular says nothing is laid by from heaven except by the decree one has made oneself, placing the apportioning in one's own former deeds.
Both make fate one's own past deeds: the Naladiyar's old deed finds its doer as a calf finds its mother among many cows; Tirumular's decree is the one 'one made oneself before'.
Both picture the body as a bird's nest or shell the life leaves; the Kural uses it to show how slight the bond of body and life is, Tirumular to say the Lord will build another nest.

The Kural asks whether the life lodging in the body has found no home of its own; Tirumular accepts the body as a passing house and draws comfort from it: losing one is like entering another, for those who know Nandi.
If 2854's 'no going, no coming' is read of the knower, both say that examining and grasping what truly is ends birth: the Kural's mind that ponders and knows what is need not think of birth again.

note: 2804 places the Lord as Om, fire and right order within the heart; 2853 goes further and says the mind and Siva are not different, Siva showing within the mind as it clears.
Both make the bliss bodily: in 2831 turiya, sweet as milk and honey, soaks every hair-root; in 2856 nectar wells up at each hair-root.
Both end on the Lord who stays as scent in a flower (மலர்க்கந்தம் ... நின்றானே); 304 sets the image after the devotee's babbling praise, 2857 after naming him as all things yet beyond thought.
The Kural names sulking and union as what lovers gain from love; Tirumular, using the same pair (புலவி, புணர்வு), says the Lord is both, carrying love's moments over to the soul and God.
2857 affirms that he is awareness, life, union; 2861 denies him every name, then reconciles the two: being all these, it is none of them.
Both call the state where turiya subsides the void where words cease (சொல்லறும் பாழ்) and say it is hard to know or tell.

Both make the one without attachment the only thing to cling to: the Kural bids one hold to his hold to let go of holding, Tirumular says the unattached hold to the Supreme and the kinless find him their kin.

In 38 the poet vows never to stop babbling Nandi's name; 2865 says those who gain his light stop babbling. If பிதற்று is the same praise in both, the vow belongs to the seeker and the silence to the one who has arrived.
Both put a single herdsman over the five (senses): 2025 has one man graze them with a staff, 2883 says that once herded and checked the five cows give milk.
The Kural guards the five with the goad of firmness and calls that man a seed for release; Tirumular herds them and they yield milk. Both make the senses useful once controlled.

The Kural says the field of the five must be destroyed (அடல், which Parimelazhagar glosses as கெடுத்தல்); Tirumular wants the five herded so they give milk. If அடல் means only 'conquer', the two agree; on the stronger reading they differ on whether the senses are ended or tamed.

Both use the man who passes over sweet fruit at hand to toil for a poor one: in 201 the jackfruit and the wild date stand for wife and another's wife; in 2901 the banana, jaggery and honey against the poisonous etti are left unnamed.
The Kural uses the ripe fruit left for the raw one for harsh speech when sweet words are at hand; Tirumular sets the sweet beside the poisonous etti, and his riddle leaves the referent open.
2872 ends with those who plough barren land with the breath-yoke; 2880 says their intent is unknowable and what sprouts in such soil may wither.
2883 has the wild cows herded so they give milk; 2903 drives the grazing cows beyond the field to the Lord's feet.
audit_text_issue: 2903's last line (கொல்லசெய் நெஞ்சம் குறியறியாதே) is obscure

note: The Kural says birth is cut only when attachment is cut; Tirumular says the bud's flowering is seen only by those who have let the bond go.
Both make the highest state a kind of sleep: in 129 the wise saw Siva-bhoga within while sleeping; here the Lord and the lady sleep in an enjoyment that has no sleep.
Both use the same phrase for the hidden way in, the ford no one knows (துறை அறியோம், துறையறிவார் இல்லை): in 1987 the breath that circles and lies plugged, here the place where devotees drew bliss.

Two arguments for the same claim, that the state is known only by having it: the mother can't tell her daughter her joy, and the taste of the fruit and the nature of a wife are known only to the eater and the husband.

Both use spreading and drawing in (விரிவு குவிவு, விரிந்து குவிந்தது): here the light beyond turiya swallows and spits out the movement; in 2981 it is the mind's movement, whose end with speech is release.

The Kural promises a world above the gods to one who cuts off the pride of 'I' and 'mine'; Tirumular describes the cutting from inside, the self, wealth, body and mind undone until even the 'I' that would notice is gone.

Both use muteness against false silence: in 1896 one whose speech alone stops is merely mute (மூங்கை) while true silence stills the mind too; here those who talk of the unspeakable are the mutes, and the Lord is seen by the mind gone still.
2718 says repeating சிவாய நம and சிவசிவ fixes the mind and is bliss; here the mantra has become a fruit already eaten, and the speaker reports its sweetness.
Both say death can be beaten by those who have the power of tapas: the Kural speaks of leaping past Yama, Tirumular of striking him with the sword of knowledge in a mind where tapas has come.
272 says only those who melt with love can reach 'my gem' (என்பொன் மணி), whatever austerity others do; here the speaker melts to the bone, weeping, and holds 'my golden gem' as his own.

note: 1823 makes the body of flesh the temple and the heart the shrine; 2982 tells the same as a story of search: those who chased the Lord across lands lost him, and the speaker found him in the body.
Both end on the same phrase, புகுந்துநின்றான்: in 27 the Lord enters the minds of those who bow to Nandi daily, in 2985 he enters and stays in his devotees' hearts.
Both make the Lord's thousand names (ஆயிர நாமம்) a practice: 34 praises them going and sitting, 2987 promises protection and the end of desire to those who recite them.
The Kural says the two kinds of deed do not cling to those devoted to the Lord's praise; Tirumular says the lord whom the worshipper keeps in mind cuts away deeds and the planets' sway.

If அள்ளற் கடல் is the sea of births, the two verses agree: the Kural's sea of births is crossed by those who reach the Lord's feet, and Tirumular's sea of mire is cut for those who proclaim his bounty.
Both set the Lord beyond those who would know him: in 13 Vishnu, Brahma and the gods cannot measure him, in 3019 the siddhas and gods think on him through all time without knowing him.
Both end with the Lord as rain: in 11 Nandi is the rain-pouring cloud, in 3021 the Lord is everywhere like rain, answering the question of where he is.

10 lists the Lord as bearer of the earth, fire, sun, moon, mountain and sea, ending தடவரை தண்கடலாமே; 3023 repeats the frame, ending தடம்கடலாமே, but grounds each line in his own strength and adds that he is lighter than an atom.

Nearly the same verse. 2857 makes the Lord union and lovers' sulking (புணரும், புலவி); 3035 makes him union and the senses (புணர்வும், புலனும்), so the love pair becomes a list of faculties he pervades. Both end on the scent in the flower cluster.

Nearly the same verse: the Lord stood where nothing could know him, and the eight worlds. 1722 ends with his taking the poet's body as his temple; 3044 ends with Nandi as the one who knows this, our lord.
Both turn on the same line, the bright flame that knows the flesh and breathes within. 1797 asks who could know the Lord if that flame did not; 3027 answers that when it knows, one can reach him.

Both place the Lord by the same four stations, within (உண்ணின்ற), in the sky (விண்ணின்று), on earth (மண்ணின்ற) and in the eye (கண்ணின்ற). 449 names him the light within and the gem in the eye; 3040 the breath within, the sun, the wind and thought.
The Kural calls number and letter (எண், எழுத்து) the eyes of living beings; Tirumular makes the Supreme their maker and goes on to the eye that takes things in. Learning's two eyes become his gift.
Both name the Lord as ஆதி, the first: the Kural makes the world have Adi Bhagavan as its first, as letters have அ; Tirumular calls Sankara 'the first, our first', present with all the world yet one.

Both open with the same line on the three thousand Tamil verses Mulan spoke. 99 makes the work Nandi's grace and promises the Lord to those who recite it; 3046 adds three hundred mantras and thirty teachings and declares the three one.
The book's frame: in 73 Tirumular puts Nandi's holy feet on his head before telling the Agama; in 3047 the work ends by blessing the same feet (நந்தி திருவடி).

Both honour the feet of the Lord named by his knowledge: the Kural's வாலறிவன் (one of pure knowledge), whose feet give learning its point, and Tirumular's மெய்ஞ்ஞானத்தவன் (one of true knowledge) and மலமிலான் (the one without impurity).
